[quote=skullsbrough;60703790]"Ah, yes, the ships! 

Here I have the request that the Department of Defense asked me to deliver."

He looks at one of his folders 

"The Department of Defense wanted to acquire at least 2 amphibious assault ships, 3 destroyers, a frigate, and a cruiser. from you. As well as at least 1 underway replenishment ship for both surface and submarine ships."

He then moves to address the second request

"I think I can do that, given my new position that I will be inaugurated into upon my return to the country. 

Your country is a reliable partner of ours. And typically, your equipment is higher quality than our own domestically produced equipment. As long as you can keep providing that, I don't see why a partnership couldn't be established. Although maybe we could negotiate a discount of sorts? Lower prices in return for greater favor?"[/quote]
"We could do a discount..." Witstrom says, pulling out his government issued phone to check something. After a few moments of moving through what appears to be pages of lists, he looks back up at Klos. "We can retrofit some ships for the replenishment role as well as deliver those destroyers and frigate. I'll have to contact some people about the cruiser, but I know that the amphibious assault ships will have to be built ordered."

He takes a large gulp from a water bottle apparently kept in his suit jacket. "I assume a partnership could be established, but you would have to guarantee the safety of some defense contractors who worked with the royalty of your nation. I assume you're aware of those rifles they imported before the revolution. Not to mention some equipment will have to be ordered directly from the factory, so if you want those, the companies will need to be reassured their property will be safe. I assume you know how it is."

[quote=oceanice_republics;60765717][i]The convoy rolled to a halt at the front entrance of the New Rorack Diplomatic Center, its glass façade gleaming under the muted afternoon light. As the doors opened, Oceanice D.E.S.F. guards stepped out first, forming a protective corridor with practiced precision.

Then came President Ironvisak Willham, dressed strikingly in the formal uniform of the old Oceanice Republic, that immediately drew subtle glances from nearby staff. Everyone inside the Diplomatic Center already knew of todays meeting; the press had gathered for days to get information about the meeting. But even with all the preparation, the sheer presence of the D.E.S.F. escort, combined with Willhams historical attire, brought a quiet tension to the hall.

A Lavian security officer approached with a welcoming gesture. 
 Welcome, Mr. President. This way, please.

He led the group forward through the expansive lobby, where models of Lavian engineering projects stood proudly on polished platforms: experimental rail systems, naval vessels, and aerospace prototypes arranged between seating areas and a pristine café buzzing with diplomatic staff.
Dr. Kals Decvier and Dr. Helena Veyra walked close behind the president, eyeing both the displays and the alert posture of the Lavian security personnel, who were clearly adjusting to the scale of the Oceanice security detail.

As they passed beneath a suspended model of an MB-157 interceptor, it caught the President's eye. Willham paused for a moment.

Look at that, he murmured. Its rare to see an old era plane preserved so well. Dr. Helena followed his gaze. A reminder, Mr. President that era is behind us. Now its time to change our history and move toward a better cause. Willham nodded, straightening his uniform as if accepting both the weight of the past and the responsibility ahead.
 Exactly. Today, we negotiate not as heirs of our nations pasts... but for a better future which we hope to lead.

The group continued onward, stepping through a secure frame into the main conference chamber. The room opened before them with polished wood paneling, warm diffused lighting, and two long rows of flags of Oceanice and Lavian standing opposite one another.[/i]

[i]After signing the cord, President Ironvisak Willham nodded toward the hall, I would like to make a speech. his voice steady.
It is time this Cold War ends. For the good of our nations and for a new generation to come. With the death of Vanklyis Adelais Herman, may his soul find rest. We, the U.S.O., have changed our path. We no longer follow the old fatherlands hatred and iron fist rule.
Today, beside me sits Dr. Kals Decvie, a fox, a citizen, a scholar welcomed among us as an equal. No more racial laws. No more chains from the Oceanice Republics past.
 The U.S.O. is a democracy that accepts all humans, or not. We hope the U.S.O. and U.L.R. preserve peace, without fear of war or worse nuclear fate.
A polite wave of chuckles moved through the room at his half-joke.
But I speak honestly, the Argos Friendship Accords begin a new era not for us, but for Argos itself.
He stepped back.
 Dr. Kals Decvie rose next.
The young fox drew in a trembling breath.
For years, this Cold War kept our peoples apart. But change came because of leaders like President Ironvisak and my mentor, Dr. Helena.
They ended a regime that dehumanized my kind, that hid crimes no one in the world ever fully saw. The monsters like Herman..
Kal suddenly grabbed his shirt and tore it open.
Gasps filled the hall. Across his furred chest lay a grotesque puckered bullet scar, and purple bruising spiraled across the ribs, proof.
Ironvisaks thoughts flashed
 This wasnt in the script. What is this kid doing!?
Out loud, he exploded*
KIDWHAT IN HELL IS WRONG WITH YOU!? This is NOT how you address an international ceremony!
But Kals eyes were wild, pained, burning.
He reached inside his coat.
He pulled out a homemade revolver.
The room went silent.
Tell them the truth, Kal hissed.
 Tell them you were o
KalNO! Dr. Helena cried, voice cracking.
 Put that away, pleaseplease!
Kals voice broke with grief.
Mother Im sorry. I cant let the man who destroyed my people stand here alive and honored!
Ironvisaks face twisted with confusion.
What? Kid, youre mistaken. I Ive done nothing like that. Im not them, and I will NEVER be them.
Kal lifted the gun higher, shaking violently.
Shut up! Youre not who they say you are, Mr. Gerich..!
Before he could finish.
BOOM!*
The reinforced doors slammed open.
A full squad of D.E.S.F. Guardians stormed in, armored exosuits hissing, visors glowing. Each soldier carried a braced Super-MG3A Hydra Support Gun, the barrels already spinning.
DOWN! DOWN NOW! PROTECT THE PRESIDENT!
Ironvisak shouted:
WAITDONT SHOOT!
But the targeting sensors had already locked.
Kals trembling hand lifted the gun a fraction of an inch.. And that was enough. The Hydra guns left gun shock.
The air tore apart*
 The glass exploded*
 Banners ripped from their poles*
 The U.L.R. delegation dove under the table as shockwaves punched through the hall.
Kal was hit instantly, his body jerking, the revolver flying from his hand.
He collapsed near the stage stairs, unmoving.
Smoke drifted upward, thick and oily.
Then
Silence.
 A silence too heavy to breathe in.
Dr. Helena screamed.
KAL! NONO, PLEASE!
She fell to her knees, clutching him, shaking uncontrollably.
Ironvisak staggered forward, pale with blood covering his shirt.
WHO AUTHORIZED THAT FIRING!? WHO GAVE THAT ORDER!?
His fist slammed the podium so hard the metal buckled.
The D.E.S.F. captain froze.
Sir he pointed a firearm at you. Threat ProtocolSection 4requires automatic neutralization.
I DIDNT GIVE THE ORDER! Ironvisak screams.
 This was a peace ceremonynot a battlefield!
U.L.R. delegates shouted in panic and fury. Cameras recorded, but were shot after the squad of D.E.S.F. guards burst open the door.
Dr. Helena sobbed over Kals body.
Kals eyes fluttered open.
Blood slipped down his mouth.
He looked at Ironvisak and with the last of his fading breath whispered
I know who you are
 Gerichmen
Ironvisak froze.
All color drained from his face.
What what did you call me?
Kals hand twitched, reaching for nothing.
His chest fell.
One final exhale.
And he went still.
The hall was silent.
Dead silent.[/i]

[b]Febuary 2, 2027: The Mother of Montfleur[/b]

As Thýven leaned ever leftward, Montfleur remained stable, at least to the international scene. Internally a silent revolution of power had occurred since Lo Pilato and Madame Terassi had made their visit on the humid summer day to speak with the king of Montfleur, and had effectively granted through polite discussion a revolutionary mandate to the Duchess Éleonore de Lorraine. 

Now as she stood on the balcony of La Palace de la Défense, the cardinal rochambeau beside her holding a fragile bible, she recalled her stern words to Lo Pilato and Terassi,   Communism, under its ideal, tears down the authority in an attempt to solve oppression, and in its stead it causes more oppression as anything against communism is seen as evil, whether it be king or president, or the man who has the extra penny.  It was now that Thýven had fallen to the revolutionary mandate, Montfleur had to traverse its own path into the revolution, not through the citharo line, but through the old ally of liberality. 

The oath of office, conferring upon her the presidency of the state council, was given in a solemn tone, and repeated in an even more serious tone, before she, in her dulcet and almost musical tone began to speak to the masses below.

[i]My friends, today I speak not as a superior of your kin or as a member of this government, but I speak as one of you, to you. 

For too long has Montfleur sat in the dying embers of the colonial era, propped up by the wealth of that era and the industry of that era. Every day our legislature claims to hear the needs of the people, yet our nation remains quiet as the world turns. 

To our south the once liberal bastion of Thýven has fallen to the throes of the peoples revolution, unaided by wiser powers, it throws itself down a path of division and federalisation, threatening even the safety of its own citizens with this venture. To the west, Daesun expands rapidly to seek its own against THEP, and the EDU strains at the ropes to lash itself into a brutal war with THEP, to the East, Shamat sits as continentalism rises in its nations and pan-shamatism becomes a firm ideology. 

Yet Montfleur merely observes these changes with mild amusement, moving not a finger, lest we fear to provoke some power or state. However, I should ask you my people, is Montfleur privy to the wishes of another state? Is it privy to the economy of another monarch, president, or council? No, I tell you Montfleur is Montfleur, and it will always belong to itself, a puppet of no-one, a fate determined only by the will of God. 

And it is the will of God that I should now become your leader, not in the patriarchal sense of leadership, but in the sense of that Thrømm who calls himself Piter Drømm, a servant of the peoples. 

Yes, I call for a new order in Montfleur, one where the worker and the people become the marchers and cogs of the state, where the old are replaced with the new, and the conductor of the state drives us forward into a brighter future. Montfleur and her people shall determine the path of the stormy seas, we shall be the light of liberalism in the world! 

Let us champion full employment as mandated by the rights of man, let us modernise our factories, our fields, our schools, let us stir ourselves out of our slumber and march forward together, with the torch of liberty held high for all to see. Montfleur advance![/i]
